name: WPP

summary.text: WPP plc is a London-based advertising and communications holding company listed in London and New York. On this site it appears as the owner of the public relations firms Hill & Knowlton and Burson Cohn & Wolfe (BCW, the successor of Burson-Marsteller). On January 25, 2024 WPP announced it would unite BCW and Hill & Knowlton into a single agency named Burson, with more than 6,000 employees in 43 markets, operating from July 1, 2024; its 2024 annual report and Form 20-F describe Burson as created in June 2024 from the merger.

facts.claim: On January 25, 2024 WPP announced that Hill & Knowlton and BCW would merge into a single agency called Burson, naming BCW global CEO Corey duBrowa as Burson's global CEO and Hill & Knowlton global chair and CEO AnnaMaria DeSalva as its global chair. The merged agency was to begin operating on July 1, 2024, with more than 6,000 employees across 43 markets.
facts.quote: WPP unites BCW and Hill & Knowlton to create Burson

sources.title: WPP unites BCW and Hill & Knowlton to create Burson, a global leader built for a new era of communications
WPP to merge BCW and Hill & Knowlton to create comms giant

facts.claim: WPP's 2024 Form 20-F and annual report state that Burson was created in June 2024 from the merger of BCW and Hill & Knowlton; the January press release had given July 1, 2024 as the operating start date.
facts.quote: Burson was created in June 2024 from the BCW and Hill & Knowlton merger

sources.title: WPP plc Form 20-F for fiscal year 2024
WPP plc Annual Report and Accounts 2024

facts.claim: Provoke Media reported that the merged firm would have revenue above $1.1 billion, that the Burson name honours Harold Burson, founder of Burson-Marsteller, and that Hill & Knowlton would continue to operate as a distinct brand within Burson for select clients, including where there may be conflicts. WPP does not disclose fee income by agency.
facts.quote: Hill & Knowlton will continue to operate as a distinct brand within Burson, serving select clients, including those where there may be conflicts

sources.title: Hello Burson: WPP merges BCW and H&K to create $1bn PR firm

facts.claim: Axios described the Burson merger as the latest round of mergers within WPP, which has long been consolidating its internal brands to streamline operations. A WPP spokesperson did not rule out job losses, saying the aim was to minimise the impact on jobs to the greatest extent possible.

openQuestions: The site's hill-and-knowlton file states H&K 'was owned by WPP'; this is supported by WPP's own January 2024 release. The date WPP acquired Hill & Knowlton (and the 1980s acquisition history) was not researched.

The 2018 formation of BCW from Burson-Marsteller and Cohn & Wolfe was not confirmed from a WPP document in the sources opened; the connection to burson-marsteller rests on PRovoke's statement about the Burson name and WPP's description of BCW.
The National Smokers Alliance and Citizens for a Free Kuwait episodes predate the 2024 merger; no WPP document on those matters was opened.
